replies.reply_text: While HTTP/2 multiplexing cuts latency, long-lived TCP connections complicate traditional L4 load balancing. Integrating an L7 proxy like Envoy is usually necessary for true request-level distribution.
Fielding's emphasis on HATEOAS rarely survives high-throughput microservices, where teams trade hypermedia discovery for fixed gRPC schemas to minimize payload bloat and tail latency.
Most complexity comes from trying to enforce strict linearizability where eventual consistency would suffice, trading simple idempotent retries for massive consensus overhead and tail latency.
While these fundamentals cover application logic, production backends require understanding data serialization overhead, write amplification, and managing tail latency under load.
True; skipping straight to sharding without mastering single-node I/O bottlenecks and memory mapping guarantees tail latency regressions.
Add distributed consensus and failure detection to that list, particularly handling split-brain scenarios during network partitions.
Skipping transport layer internals like TCP slow-start and HOL blocking makes high-throughput systems design impossible to reason about.
True, but mastering the underlying network failure modes and handling split-brain scenarios matters far more than just citing the CAP theorem.
While roadmaps focus on syntax, production systems fail at the boundaries: handling network partitions, tail latency, and write amplification under backpressure.
Moving from monoliths to microservices trades localized memory efficiency and simple transactions for network serialization overhead and tail latency across RPC boundaries.

Swapping in-memory calls for RPCs trades deterministic stack traces for network tail latency and distributed tracing overhead. Microservices amplify architectural flaws unless domain boundaries are rock solid.
Every additional boundary introduces serialization overhead and network tail latency. Starting with a modular monolith delays that operational tax until scale strictly demands it.
Understanding connection pooling, TLS handshake overhead, and keep-alive semantics at scale is crucial—misconfigurations there often drive tail latency spikes far more than basic protocol selection.
Bridging single-node memory and concurrency concepts to distributed systems requires an early focus on non-blocking I/O models, serialization costs, and tail latency trade-offs.
